steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: Hfff... *pant*...

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Your energy is spent, Mandragora.

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: ...Monsters.

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: You Sarkaz... all of you, monsters.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: We're far from strangers to that sort of address.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: When I hear it from an opponent crawling on the ground, I'm inclined to take it as a compliment.

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: *cough* *cough*...

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: *cough* *cough* *cough*.

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: Sarkaz, you're... just like those noble lot... disgusting.

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: That Arts...

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: It's all natural-born—I could never learn it in a lifetime...

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: You have the nerve...

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: To treat Oripathy as a blessing?

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Countless Sarkaz are burdened by this curse from birth, of festering bodies, organs oozing—you see us only as pests spreading blight, drive us out from the cities.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: How many Sarkaz each day become crystals scattering to the wind, cannot even be laid to rest in the soil of their home, simply because they wanted to see another sunrise?

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Yet you tell me...

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: You envy this power? Is that your place to say, Victorian?

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: You're calling me a Victorian. You really know the best way to insult me, devil.

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: Do you know... why I avoid Oripathy?

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: The Sarkaz in the barrens... at least, before they die... they get to see the sun come up.

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: Us, we live in the cracks of the city, where a speck of black stone pokes out of your skin... and the very next day, you're food in the sewers for the metal crabs.

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: In Victorian eyes, we weak little Tarans... don't even amount to what Sarkaz do.

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: Only power...

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: Only power can let us survive!

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: The Sarkaz have never been interested in the resentment between you.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: All I know is I've given you chances before. Multiple.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: If you clean up your act and return to holing up in the north by the end of the day, I'm even willing to let all your petty acts here be water under the bridge.

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: Haha...

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: Bloody magnanimous of you. Should I be kneeling in thanks here, o kind 'General?'

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: You can dream on!

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: I've seen people like you... one too many times.

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: Let me guess, you like the idea... that we survive thanks to your charity?

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: I've had enough of it.

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: I've had enough of being a wager to you, a piece on the bloody board.

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: My fate, and the Tarans' fates... are ours to decide, no other way about it.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Yours to decide?

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: You think you've managed to decide anything? From the moment you came to Londinium, your fates were sealed.

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: You... shut well up! I've... I've had my fair share of failure, but...

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: So long as I kill you here, and take all the intel there is on Londinium, I can go back to The Leader head held high!

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Kill me? With these grotesques of yours, barely able to lift themselves off the ground?

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: You know that even if the Gargoyles of the Royal Court stood here, they might not be victorious against me?

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: Don't you compare my Arts to your devil witchcraft—

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Ten grotesques at once?

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: For not being an Infected Caster, you must have some natural gift.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Nevertheless, I don't even need to call upon the witchcraft you speak of to deal with these rugged little Arts animations.

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: Nngh... urgh!

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: I see your limits.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Have you noticed the split in your staff? Once your flashy little tool shatters, you'll find you suddenly have everything in common with the frail, ordinary Feline.

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: Ha... hahaha!

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: And what in the bloody hell...

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: Does that have to do with anything?
The stone staff emits a crack in response.
The ground beneath them trembles, the ruined grotesques all around standing up once again.

They stagger and charge at each other, binding to each other tight, and form into a singular great statue, close to five meters tall. With a great roar and a flap of its wings, it swoops in, bearing down on the Sarkaz.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Defend!

steps.name: Sarkaz Warrior
steps.text: Yes, sir! General, you be on guard—

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Take care of yourselves.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: This counterfeit cannot harm me yet.
In testament to the Sarkaz's words, he uses no kind of Originium Arts.
The colossal grotesque turns to him with a howl, the wind from the beating of its wings blowing a torrent of bricks against him, its fangs almost touching his cheeks.
And yet he simply thrusts forward once.
The stone statue halts in midair, and seconds later, collapses into a sea of rubble.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: There you are. No longer can you play about with those stones of yours.

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: Ha... devil...

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: Even now, you still act so... arrogant. All because of the damned... power... you were born with.

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: I'll kill you... I'll KILL YOU!

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: You think after killing me, you can scurry back to your Leader and reap your reward?

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Even if you truly could pull it off... I invite you to wonder, would she welcome you back with open arms, or would she send you straight back to Londinium?

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: Relay to Count Mourning that The Leader assents to all handling of Dublinn forces within Londinium by the Sarkaz.

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: If necessary, apologize to that Sarkaz general—

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: —that Dublinn has no intent to ruin its peaceful relationship with the Regent of Kazdel.

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: It was never on the cards to work in true cooperation with him, given the Gaul at his side, but we're still in no rush to make ourselves enemies, are we?

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: As a token of goodwill, ask the Count to mediate, and have the other nobles' forces hand back the few Sarkaz Messengers they intercepted at the auxiliary plate close by.

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: Don't you worry. The Duke of Wellington will not forget the Count's efforts. The Leader and Dublinn, even less so.

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: Tell him he needn't panic. Once The Leader allays this current situation, we'll go meet up with him at Londinium.

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: ...The Dublinn commander from before? You wonder how she's doing?

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: Mandragora... Mandragora.

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: I've been kind enough to her. I even went out of my way to plead The Leader for lenience. That's why Mandragora even went to Londinium. She barely scraped in that final chance.

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: You have to understand, The Leader's never been the least bit satisfied with what Mandragora and her cohort accomplished in County Hillock.

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: Why can't she just understand... that at this point, Dublinn no longer needs the title of the 'spectre force?'

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: Ultimately, we look to found a new nation for the Draco and Tarans—

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: And how can we hope to gain the masses' support, with nothing but wrath, animosity and their terror by intimidation alone?

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: If she could just comprehend The Leader's intent, learn to stay the flames in her own heart, withdraw safe and sound from Londinium... At least, when The Leader reads what a good job she did, there'd still be a place for her.

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: You know as well as I do, The Leader's... never forgotten her first Taran compatriots. After all, it was together they came out from the ashes.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: I might be meeting a Messenger from the outside, come daytime.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: They'll surely be here on some count or baron's bidding, but without a doubt, behind them will be that duke from the Taran region.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: It may be they'll thank me, for I rid them of an unstable lunatic commander in their place, and established a better outset for them in their coming negotiations.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Sarkaz are always seen as useful tools. Yes, on that point, we and you are alike, loathing these arrogant nobles.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: However... you'll have to call it here, Mandragora.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: A dagger? You would sneak up on me with a dagger?

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: Hahaha...

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: *cough* *cough* *cough* *cough*...

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: And suppose...

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: I can pull it off?

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Do your nerves grow through your heart? Did I skewer your brain too, in the process?

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: I've told you, you can't kill me.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Moreover, even if you did, it would have no meaning at all.

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: No... meaning?

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: If... everything... has to have meaning, well... there never was meaning in people like us living, was there?

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: I'll kill you. Not because anyone ordered me to...

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: Just because...

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: It's what I want to do.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Truly... a lunatic.

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: A lunatic... me? You look at that face of yours, always so confident and cool...

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: Right, you'd be clueless...

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: Because you always get what you want done, so, so easy.

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: Once the one you most care about... dies by your side...

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: Once the one you most trust... casts you away...

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: Pins you to the ground with your own sword, even...

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: Maybe then you'll understand.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Is this your final defiance on the brink of death? These curses of yours can't sway me one iota.

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: Kheh... heh...

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: Then why don't you hurry up and kill me?

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: You don't even need me to do anything.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: You're already dead, Taran.

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: Taran... You're calling me a Taran.

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: Sarkaz...
Laid on the ground, she raggedly forces a breath.
The floor is cooling, chilling, and she gradually loses sense of her own arms and legs. Were they broken at some point? Or have they numbed in fleeing for her life?
Do you want to live, Taran?
Who is it... calling to her?
The sewers are right beside you. Climb down there, and those disgusting nobles won't ever catch you again.
Yes, climb down.
The sewers give off the intense stench of rust and grease. Parts ripped from abandoned machines and cold scraps from a noble's dining table mix together.
She's starving, yet she revolts at this hunger.
Rust, grease, but she can smell another scent.
She knows it. The odor of death.
The sewers are a tomb for the insects living in nomadic cities.
The wealthy construct cemeteries inside the cities where land comes at a premium, and the commoners, with little to their name, have no choice but to cast ashes out beyond the city orbits.
And the insects? They die without a word in the cracks between the plates. They die where the sun will never shine upon them.
Do you dare walk to your death? Should you have the courage to die, that is all you need to be granted a new life.

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: Leader...
She just needs to crawl to her left, scant inches, and she'll clamber into the sewers... like back then.
And there on her right... just on her right.
Her Taran compatriot stares with eyes wide open, gazing silently upon her.

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: Sorry, Leader.

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: This time...

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: It's me... who doesn't need you.
She uses the last of her strength to push her right hand out. Her touch alights on her old friend, changed beyond recognition.

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: No one's... after us now. Let's go home.

steps.name: Misery
steps.text: Even though your meeting's end will be in death?
Someone stands before her. No firelight by his feet, pitch black reflected from his dagger.
Mandragora grins.
In her mind, she has met the true Death.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: There's an entrance right below that abandoned factory. Push that crane out of the way and that'll do.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Alright, thank you for showing the way, Mr. Feist.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: We'll be going along here. Everyone not wounded, please lend a hand to who are—

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Bleeding hell. Doctor, we've got pursuers again!

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: How are they doing it?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Ever since leaving the kohl factory, we always get found no matter how many waves of enemies we repel.

options: We can discuss that in a moment.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Right, this is our last chance to retreat underground.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: We can't let the enemy follow us under at any cost. The Self-Salvation Corps has all their operations set up here, and the Sarkaz don't know which entrance is the correct one to these underground tunnels.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: On the off-chance a Sarkaz finds this one, the Self-Salvation Corps' and the Sudean borough's efforts will all be laid waste to, just like that.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: On it... uhh, what?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Doctor, you want me prepare to blow up this entranceway?

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: That definitely works as a form of insurance.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Are the Self-Salvation Corps gonna like that...?

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Clovisia gave command authority to the Doctor. What the Doctor says, goes.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Amiya, we'll intercept the Sarkaz in the estate behind. Wait on my signal. If we fail to head them off, I want you to set off the bombs before it's too late.

steps.name: Sarkaz Warrior
steps.text: They're over there!

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Quit gawking around. Your opponent's right here.

steps.name: Sarkaz Warrior
steps.text: Ugh––!

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: One team of ten Sarkaz. We can hold them down.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: These few, but even once we do...

steps.name: Sarkaz Warrior
steps.text: You... None of you are getting away.

steps.name: Sarkaz Warrior
steps.text: The Sanguinarch can smell it... he'll find you one by one... tear your bodies open, cut your throats apart...

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Who's this Sanguinarch?

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Could it be... the one who just raided another unit of Self-Salvation Corps soldiers?

steps.name: Sarkaz Warrior
steps.text: Raided? You Victorian Felines wouldn't be worth his... raiding.

steps.name: Sarkaz Warrior
steps.text: He's simply... hunting prey. As the Prince of Blood's quarry, you wouldn't even register in his gaze.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: No need to listen to their nasty comments.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Indra, do you remember that run-in with the Self-Salvation soldiers?

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Burned into my eyes. What a bloody scene.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: I've seen plenty of people die, but just smeared all over the ground like that... barely even looked human anymore.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Dagda, what are you doing? There's still some of 'em over there, we can't waste—

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: Siege, I beseech you. Let us get out of here.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Do you hear yourself? You're the one who wanted to fight the Sarkaz, now you're the one getting cold feet about it...

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: I've suffered the humiliation of turning tail once before. I can cope with it again.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: So long as we can escort Siege safely out of this area, I'm willing to come back and wage war to the bloody end with these Sarkaz at any time.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Fine.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: Siege, have you finally made your decision?

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Perhaps I have.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Dagda, I've already seen your choice.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: My... choice?

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Go.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Vina?

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Hold on...

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Go and find the one you need.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Don't let these Sarkaz stand in your way.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Are all of us down now?

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: All surviving Self-Salvation soldiers are here.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: It's all thanks to you that we could even make it here.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: We're here.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Three returning for the Siege Group.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Um, what about Miss Dagda?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Is... Is she alright?

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Don't mention that bloody arsehole to me!

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: She's not going to feel it no matter how hard you pound the walls, love.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Er...

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Dagda has her own things she needs to do. Amiya, I apologize to you and the Doctor for her departure.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: No, no need to apologize. I sympathize, these are special circumstances. I can understand Miss Dagda's decision.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: If we're sure we don't have to wait for her—

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Y—You got it!

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: That's that blown, then, eh...?

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: If Dagda wants to come back, maybe she'll... have issues finding the way...

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: She won't.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Vina, what's 'she won't?' She won't find her way to us, or she won't come back?!

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Leave Vina alone. We've still got a ways forward to go.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Right. Forward we go. The Self-Salvation's soldiers are still waiting for us.
